summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — MT.AS +6%, AALB.AS +5%, EOAN.DE +4%, BESI.AS +4%, ASM.AS +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (STLAP.PA -3%, ENT.L -2%, G24.DE -2%, RHM.DE -2%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: MT.AS (+5.89%) — EU steel import-quota tightening (eff. Jul 1) plus BofA PT hike to $80 and AWS/XCarb supply deal drove a multi-catalyst re-rating. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — ArcelorMittal is a large-cap EU cyclical/materials (steel) name; bot's uk-eu universe likely excludes commodity/steel sector or Euronext Amsterdam dual-listings entirely, not just filtered on signal.

top_movers.catalyst: EU steel import-quota tightening (eff. Jul 1) plus BofA PT hike to $80 and AWS/XCarb supply deal drove a multi-catalyst re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ArcelorMittal is a large-cap EU cyclical/materials (steel) name; bot's uk-eu universe likely excludes commodity/steel sector or Euronext Amsterdam dual-listings entirely, not just filtered on signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU materials/steel large-caps (e.g. MT.AS) to the uk-eu universe screen, or add a policy-catalyst gate that flags names with same-week regulatory/tariff announcements for next-day inclusion review.

top_movers.catalyst: Q1 2026 trading update (5 Jul): revenue €772m (+2.8% organic), EBITA margin rose to 14.2% from 13.6%, positive 2026 guidance reaffirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Aalberts is a ~€6-7B Dutch mid-cap industrial on Euronext Amsterdam, a cap/sector bucket (mid-cap industrials) the uk-eu strategies don't currently scan.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-calendar watchlist that temporarily pulls in non-universe mid-caps (>€3B) with a scheduled trading update, flagging next-day names with post-print gap ≥5% for review.

top_movers.catalyst: German government agreed a grid-reform package (faster approvals, digitalization, binding connection deadlines) seen as a positive for grid operators like E.ON; stock broke its 100-day line.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — EOAN.DE is a large-cap German utility/grid operator, a sector/geography (uk-eu regulated utilities) not currently covered by the bot's tradable universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU regulated utilities (e.g. DAX utility names like EOAN.DE) to the universe with a policy-catalyst gate that flags government infrastructure/regulatory announcements affecting grid operators.

top_movers.catalyst: No firm-specific news — broad European chip-sector rally (ASML +3%, ASMI +8%) on dovish Fed rate-cut bets after weak US jobs data, plus a rebound from this week's hybrid-bonding-delay selloff.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BESI.AS is a mid-cap Euronext Amsterdam semicap-equipment name, likely excluded because uk-eu universes are scoped to large-cap/index-constituent lists rather than semiconductor-equipment niche tickers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add BESI.AS and its AEX semicap peers (ASMI.AS) to the uk-eu universe's tech/semiconductor watchlist so sector-correlated rallies (ASML/ASMI beta >0.8) are captured, not just index-member names.

top_movers.catalyst: No single hard headline — sector-wide re-rating in semicap names ahead of ASML's July 15 earnings, plus a July 4 analyst upgrade (Zacks Buy) on rising 2026 capex/AI-upcycle estimates.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — ASM.AS is a large-cap Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker (AEX constituent, ~€40B+ mkt cap) that simply isn't on the uk-eu universe's whitelist, so no filter ever evaluated it today.
top_movers.suggestion: Widen the uk-eu universe from a static ticker list to auto-include AEX/major EU index constituents above a market-cap floor, so names like ASM.AS enter the tradable set without manual onboarding.

top_movers.catalyst: Edenred confirmed BC Partners-led investors approached it about a take-private buyout, extending the M&A speculation rally that began 2026-06-18.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — EDEN.PA is a ~€4.9B French small/mid-cap name still weighed down by Brazil/Italy regulatory reforms; its pop is binary M&A rumor speculation, not the fundamentals/momentum signal type the bot's universes screen for.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a watch-only tier for EU small/mid-cap 'take-private exploring consortium' wire hits so the bot flags these for manual review instead of full systematic entry, given binary deal-break risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued fallout from HSBC's Jul-3 downgrade to 'Reduce' (PT cut to €4 from €5.50) on swollen 93-day US dealer inventory and 19 recalls covering 2.5M vehicles YTD.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — STLAP.PA is a EUR-denominated Euronext Paris large-cap automaker; the uk-eu region universe likely screens mainly LSE/UK tickers and doesn't ingest CAC40/Paris-listed names.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend the uk-eu universe screen to include major Euronext Paris (CAC40) constituents alongside LSE names, so EUR-denominated large caps like STLAP.PA are eligible for the news-reactive strategy.

top_movers.catalyst: No firm-specific news found for 2026-07-06; move likely reflects the ongoing UK gambling-tax overhang (remote gaming duty rising 21%→40% from Apr 2026) rather than a fresh catalyst.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Entain is large-cap FTSE-100/250, so exclusion is likely a sector screen (gambling/betting names often carved out for ESG/regulatory-risk reasons), not a cap or liquidity filter.
top_movers.suggestion: If sector exclusion is intentional, no change; if it's incidental, add a carve-in for large-cap UK gambling names with a regulatory-tax-risk tag so mean-reversion strategies can trade budget/tax-driven selloffs distinct from ESG-screened long-term holds.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst — Scout24 (G24.DE) has been the DAX's biggest single-day loser repeatedly this week, extending a downtrend in place since Oct 2025 (~-30%); likely technical/sector drift, not a discrete event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. Scout24 is a real-estate/classifieds digital marketplace (ImmoScout24) only added to the DAX in Sept 2025; bot's uk-eu large-cap universe lists likely haven't been refreshed to include this recent index addition, so no strategy ever screens it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a periodic index-membership sync (e.g. refresh DAX/FTSE/CAC constituent lists monthly) so recently-added large-caps like Scout24 (DAX since 2025-09-22) enter the tradable universe automatically instead of relying on a stale snapshot.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued fallout from Germany scrapping the €12.8B F126 frigate program (Rheinmetall as lead contractor) plus JPMorgan's Jul 3 downgrade to Hold amid sector-wide defense de-rating on Ukraine/Mideast peace hopes.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — RHM.DE is a large-cap German defense/industrials name; uk-eu universes likely scope to broader indices or sectors that exclude single-name European defense primes.
top_movers.suggestion: Add top European defense primes (RHM.DE, HO.PA, BA.L) to the uk-eu universe given their outsized, headline-driven volatility this cycle, gated by a minimum liquidity/market-cap filter.
